aspects.says: Abstract methods suit complex per-constant logic, functional fields suit simple transformations.
aspects.reason: a design judgement no test can observe; the calculator and text-transforms practices build one of each

aspects.says: A constant with a body is an anonymous subclass, so getClass() is not the enum and getDeclaringClass() is.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
section:Q3: How do constant-specific method bodies work?

aspects.says: values() makes a new array on every call, so a hot path caches it, without handing the cache to callers who could change it.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: A constant-specific body overrides an abstract method, so each constant carries its own implementation.
basis: section:Q3: How do constant-specific method bodies work?

aspects.says: EnumSet and EnumMap are preferred over HashSet and HashMap for enum keys.
aspects.reason: practised on 7.2.5, whose permissions and access-index practices use EnumSet and EnumMap

aspects.says: A constant can take a lambda such as a UnaryOperator as a constructor argument and apply it, which implements the Strategy pattern.
basis: section:Q1: How do you implement the Strategy pattern using parameterized enum constants?

aspects.says: Enum fields should be final, and mutable state inside a constant breaks thread safety.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: a data race on a shared constant cannot be forced deterministically; every practice on this page keeps its fields final

aspects.says: A static map built after the constants exist gives an O(1) lookup by a parameter such as a code, returning an Optional.
basis: section:Q4: How do you create fast lookup methods for parameterized enums?

aspects.says: A nullable constructor parameter is exposed as an Optional instead of a null.
Each constant with its own body must handle its own edge cases, such as a zero divisor.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: Constructor parameters give each constant its own immutable state, and methods on the enum derive behavior from that state.
basis: section:Q2: Explain the Planet enum pattern and its advantages over plain constants.

aspects.says: An enum constructor is implicitly private and cannot be public or protected.
Enum constants are serialized by name only, and deserialization returns the existing constant.
basis: section:Q5: How does enum serialization handle parameterized constants?
aspects.reason: already asked on 7.2.1, whose quiz covers what a deserialized constant's fields hold

aspects.says: Static fields of an enum are initialized after all constants are created, so a constructor cannot use them.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
